diagrams.title: One Order, One Evidence Trail, One Settlement
diagrams.subtitle: Separate passenger transport and specimen handling within one dispatch desk.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The pod coordinates contracted providers rather than owning a fleet. Passenger trips and specimen movements require separate service rules, escalation procedures, and evidence packets.
diagrams.caption: Close each assignment only after reconciling authorization, performance evidence, payer billing, and provider settlement.

stages.label: Validate the contracted order
stages.value: Confirm payer, service scope, authorization, and collection terms
stages.detail: For NEMT, verify member eligibility, authorized transport level, destination, and standing-order validity. For courier work, verify specimen class, receiving hours, packaging responsibility, and contracted pickup deadline.

stages.label: Match qualified transport capacity
stages.value: Assign an eligible provider with documented backup coverage
stages.detail: Check driver credentials, vehicle suitability, insurance, service-area limits, and exclusions. A signed owner-operator agreement does not resolve worker classification.

stages.label: Dispatch and capture service events
stages.value: Record timestamped pickup, movement, delivery, and exceptions
stages.detail: Use RouteGenie or MediRoutes for configured NEMT GPS events. Use barcode custody records for specimens; escalate missed STAT pickups to the named laboratory contact immediately.

stages.label: Build the payer evidence packet
stages.value: Reconcile ordered service against completed service before billing
stages.detail: Scrub 837P claims only where the payer requires that format; otherwise submit the contracted broker file or courier invoice. Attach required trip verification or custody evidence.

stages.label: Collect, settle, and reconcile
stages.value: Track receivables separately from provider payment obligations
stages.detail: Forecast Medicaid broker Net-30/45 collection exposure against settlement dates. Under the canonical model, 55% of gross billings funds drivers and 45% remains before pod costs and owner profit.

diagrams.title: Convert a Defined Account Cohort
diagrams.subtitle: One hundred target accounts narrow to five signed service accounts.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative counts follow one account cohort across a complete sales cycle; they are not observed conversion benchmarks. Every later stage is a subset of the preceding stage. First-deal planning remains 2–5 months, not one sprint.
diagrams.caption: Count accounts consistently: route reviews, proposals, and awards refer to the same original account list.

stages.label: Mapped target accounts
stages.value: 100 accounts with named purchasing or transport contacts
stages.detail: Build a deduplicated list of Medicaid transport brokers, workers'-comp administrators, laboratories, and collection networks within the service territory.

stages.label: Qualified service fit
stages.value: 60 accounts pass territory, service, and payer screening
stages.detail: Retain 60% of the original cohort after confirming outsourcing demand, procurement access, credentialing requirements, and feasible payment terms.

stages.label: Documented route discovery
stages.value: 30 accounts share usable service and exception requirements
stages.detail: Advance 50% of qualified accounts after receiving trip windows, route density, transport levels, specimen needs, or other service-specific workload evidence.

stages.label: Costed proposals delivered
stages.value: 15 accounts receive capacity-backed pricing and service terms
stages.detail: Advance 50% of discovery accounts after pricing driver settlements, deadhead, standby coverage, failed pickups, and collection timing.

stages.label: Signed service accounts
stages.value: 5 accounts execute scoped contracts with operating contacts
stages.detail: Convert one-third of proposals and 5% of the original cohort. Signing does not equal dispatch readiness, recognized revenue, or collected cash.

diagrams.title: Base Case: $925,000 Gross to $166,500 Owner Profit
diagrams.subtitle: Six bars distinguish billings, retained contribution, costs, and profit.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Annual USD. Opening, retained subtotal, and closing bars are absolute totals; negative bars are deductions. Retained share is 45%. The two pod-cost allocations are illustrative splits of the canonical $249,750 residual operating cost.
diagrams.caption: $925,000 − $508,750 = $416,250 retained; $416,250 − $120,000 − $129,750 = $166,500 profit. Profit is 18.0% of gross billings and 40.0% of retained revenue.

stages.label: Opening gross contracted billings
stages.value: $925,000 annual customer billings before driver settlements
stages.detail: Opening total: NEMT brokerage and medical courier service billings, excluding underlying healthcare charges and any unrelated client transaction volume.

stages.label: Deduct external driver settlements
stages.value: −$508,750 paid to contracted transport delivery providers
stages.detail: Deduction: 55% of gross billings compensates the external transport network. These providers are separate from the four-person administrative and dispatch pod.

stages.label: Retained dispatch revenue subtotal
stages.value: $416,250 retained under the canonical 45% share
stages.detail: Absolute subtotal, not another inflow. This model uses the specified ASC 606 agent presentation; actual net presentation requires a contract-specific principal-agent assessment and is not established by the percentage alone.

stages.label: Deduct full-time pod seat costs
stages.value: −$120,000 allocated to two full-time operating seats
stages.detail: Deduction: illustrative combined compensation and employment burden for the two full-time seats. If the owner fills a seat, keep seat compensation distinct from the residual owner-profit line.

stages.label: Deduct remaining pod operating costs
stages.value: −$129,750 covers contractor seats and other operating expenses
stages.detail: Deduction: illustrative aggregate for two contractor seats, dispatch software, insurance, billing support, credentialing, administration, and service exceptions. Do not deduct driver settlements a second time.

stages.label: Closing annual owner net profit
stages.value: $166,500 equals 18.0% gross and 40.0% retained margin
stages.detail: Closing total: canonical Base-Case annual owner profit. Working-capital funding is a cash requirement rather than an additional expense automatically deducted here.

diagrams.title: Compare Retained Dollars per Completed Assignment
diagrams.subtitle: Five service examples use the same 45% retained-share assumption.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Synthetic pricing examples, not fee schedules or market quotes. Each bar measures USD retained before pod overhead for one completed one-way trip or one defined courier run. Assignment duration and mileage differ, so bars do not rank hourly returns.
diagrams.caption: Apply the contracted unit definition before comparing yield; a courier run and a passenger trip are not interchangeable units.

stages.label: Medicaid broker ambulatory trip
stages.value: $31.50 retained from a $70 completed one-way trip
stages.detail: $70 gross less $38.50 driver settlement leaves $31.50. Use broker authorization and trip-log rules; disputed eligibility or missing GPS evidence can erase collection.

stages.label: Medicaid broker wheelchair trip
stages.value: $54 retained from a $120 completed one-way trip
stages.detail: $120 gross less $66 driver settlement leaves $54. Verify vehicle equipment, securement capability, passenger assistance requirements, and the authorized transport level.

stages.label: Workers'-comp administrator trip
stages.value: $45 retained from a $100 completed one-way trip
stages.detail: $100 gross less $55 driver settlement leaves $45. Confirm administrator authorization and contracted wait-time rules rather than importing Medicaid billing assumptions.

stages.label: Scheduled laboratory courier run
stages.value: $40.50 retained from a $90 defined collection run
stages.detail: $90 gross less $49.50 driver settlement leaves $40.50. Specify included stops, receiving cutoffs, packaging responsibility, and custody-event evidence in the route scope.

stages.label: Contracted STAT specimen run
stages.value: $81 retained from a $180 defined urgent run
stages.detail: $180 gross less $99 driver settlement leaves $81. Price backup availability and deadline exposure; higher dollars per run do not establish better utilization.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before Accepting a Live Assignment
diagrams.subtitle: A failed applicable check routes the order to remediation, not dispatch.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Apply checks in sequence to the actual service. Passenger-only work does not inherit specimen-shipping requirements. Document why a conditional requirement does or does not apply.
diagrams.caption: Proceed only when the assigned provider, information workflow, service evidence, and handling method support the contracted work.

stages.label: Payer and provider eligibility
stages.value: Yes: continue; no: obtain required credentials and authorization
stages.detail: For Medicaid work, verify state and broker enrollment, driver and vehicle requirements, exclusions screening, and trip authorization under applicable program rules. 42 CFR 431.53 and 440.170(a) establish context, not universal broker payment eligibility.

stages.label: Worker status and insured capacity
stages.value: Yes: continue; no: redesign staffing or replace capacity
stages.detail: Evaluate actual control and applicable labor tests under 29 U.S.C. 203 and state law, including California Labor Code section 2775 where relevant. Verify commercial coverage for the assigned service; a 1099 label or insurance certificate alone does not resolve exposure.

stages.label: Protected information handling
stages.value: Yes: continue; no: repair access controls and required agreements
stages.detail: Determine business-associate status under 45 CFR 160.103; execute required agreements under 164.502(e) and 164.504(e). Restrict dispatch access to necessary information. A courier conduit analysis does not automatically extend to a platform storing protected health information.

stages.label: Specimen classification and exposure controls
stages.value: Yes: release; no: correct packaging or select qualified service
stages.detail: For specimen work, confirm classification before applying 49 CFR 173.199 Category B packaging and marking rules; Category A material needs a different workflow. Apply 29 CFR 1910.1030 to covered employee exposure and follow laboratory handling instructions under 42 CFR 493.1242.

diagrams.title: Four Core Seats, Six at Scaled Volume
diagrams.subtitle: Two full-time and two contractor seats expand to three of each.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each bar represents one distinct pod seat; the final two seats activate only in the Scaled scenario. External drivers are delivery capacity outside the pod count. Contractor designation requires a supportable relationship under applicable law.
diagrams.caption: Base capacity is not round-the-clock staffing. Sell only coverage windows supported by the roster and documented backup arrangements.

stages.label: Core FT: owner and account lead
stages.value: One full-time seat owns contracts, capacity, and cash
stages.detail: Approve pricing, review receivable aging, maintain payer relationships, and own escalation decisions. Separate operating seat compensation from residual owner profit.

stages.label: Core FT: dispatch operations lead
stages.value: One full-time seat owns live routing and service evidence
stages.detail: Manage RouteGenie or MediRoutes workflows, provider availability, missed pickups, and shift handoffs. Protect specimen and passenger workflows from accidental mixing.

stages.label: Core C: claims and collections specialist
stages.value: One contractor seat owns billing quality and receivable follow-up
stages.detail: Validate required 837P fields or broker invoice files, resolve denials, reconcile remittances, and escalate Net-30/45 slippage before settlement cash becomes constrained.

stages.label: Core C: credential and quality specialist
stages.value: One contractor seat owns provider records and evidence sampling
stages.detail: Track credential expiration, insurance evidence, trip-log completeness, and barcode custody exceptions. Structure the engagement around a lawful service relationship.

stages.label: Scaled FT: second operations dispatcher
stages.value: One additional full-time seat extends supported coverage windows
stages.detail: Add this seat for the canonical three-FT configuration as concurrent assignments and recovery workload exceed the documented capacity of the core operations lead.

stages.label: Scaled C: route onboarding specialist
stages.value: One additional contractor seat implements newly awarded service routes
stages.detail: Add this seat for the canonical three-contractor configuration; document stop instructions, provider readiness, laboratory contacts, and route acceptance evidence.

diagrams.title: Allocate Startup Capital Without Buying a Fleet
diagrams.subtitle: Four buckets total $40,000 within the $15,000–$65,000 range.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values show a $40,000 planning case. Corresponding lean allocations total $15,000 and expanded allocations total $65,000. These are funding envelopes, not automatically deductible expenses or proof of sufficient payment float.
diagrams.caption: At Base-Case driver settlements of $508,750 annually, smooth 30-day exposure is approximately $41,815 and 45-day exposure is $62,723 before offsets from actual settlement terms.

stages.label: Provider readiness and insurance setup
stages.value: $12,000 planning allocation for service-ready provider onboarding
stages.detail: Lean allocation $3,000; expanded allocation $18,000. Fund coverage deposits, credential checks, contract setup, and provider onboarding rather than vehicle purchases.

stages.label: Dispatch and evidence infrastructure
stages.value: $8,000 planning allocation for configured operational tooling
stages.detail: Lean allocation $2,000; expanded allocation $12,000. Fund dispatch configuration, barcode equipment, access controls, billing integration, and event-record retention.

stages.label: Commercial setup and pilot preparation
stages.value: $9,000 planning allocation for contracting and service preparation
stages.detail: Lean allocation $3,000; expanded allocation $15,000. Fund scoped route discovery, staff preparation, dry runs, payer setup, and account acquisition before live volume.

stages.label: Settlement cash and exception reserve
stages.value: $11,000 planning allocation held for timing and recovery exposure
stages.detail: Lean allocation $7,000; expanded allocation $20,000. Size final liquidity from daily settlements and collection lags. This reserve alone cannot fund Base-Case 30-day driver exposure; stage volume or secure additional liquidity.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to an Evidence-Ready Operating Desk
diagrams.subtitle: Four weekly milestones prepare the business for a 2–5 month sales cycle.
diagrams.assumptions_note: This sprint establishes readiness, not a promised first award. Use synthetic or properly authorized test records; do not dispatch paid passenger or specimen work before applicable credentials, agreements, and service requirements are satisfied.
diagrams.caption: Preserve the canonical annual cases: Conservative $250,000 gross and $30,000 profit; Base $925,000 and $166,500; Scaled $1,600,000 and $384,000. The sprint does not forecast those results.

stages.label: Days 1-7: define the service boundary
stages.value: Complete territory, payer, provider, and service requirement maps
stages.detail: Choose initial NEMT transport levels and courier specimen classes. Document enrollment requirements, insurance coverage, labor classification, pickup windows, and accountable exception contacts.

stages.label: Days 8-14: configure the evidence path
stages.value: Demonstrate order intake through dispatch, custody, and billing records
stages.detail: Configure dispatch roles, GPS events, barcode custody records, required information agreements, and payer-specific billing outputs. Test missing authorization and missed pickup cases with controlled records.

stages.label: Days 15-21: validate capacity and unit economics
stages.value: Finish provider-backed route quotes and settlement timing models
stages.detail: Model 45% retained share: Conservative $112,500 retained with $30,000 profit at 26.67%; Base $416,250 retained with $166,500 profit at 40.0%; Scaled $720,000 retained with $384,000 profit at 53.33%. Gross margins remain 12%, 18.0%, and 24%, respectively.

stages.label: Days 22-30: rehearse and pursue scoped awards
stages.value: Complete exception drills, account proposals, and operating handoffs
stages.detail: Rehearse driver absence, disputed trip evidence, missed STAT pickup, and late remittance. Assign the four core seats and define when the two Scaled seats are needed. Submit proposals without treating unsigned pipeline as revenue.
